items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: Ada Ward was her name, the prima donna of the show, and she was trying to get the band fired because the band they had before, she was going with one of the guys in the band.

ctx.x: Was this at the Cotton Club?

It was the Cotton Club. And the manager of the Cotton Club kept telling her, he says, "If I was you, I wouldn't bother the band. You're making yourself being hated. Why don't you leave the band alone? They're doing a good job." And Ada, "They can't play for me. They can't do nothing for me. They're just ruining my songs."

So then that new show come in because of the new band. So her part, she come out, she's got to have a big obbligato in front, you know, just she and the fiddle. So Otto Hardwick says, "We got her now." So, just before show time the guy left the fiddle on the piano, Otto Hardwick got some soap and dampened it and soaped the bow, you know, and soaped the bow up good.
